swaps.old_row: | J-A67.61 | Chose to draw a Works' duration inside its `WorksTable` row's range (a small timber house 2–6 weeks, a stone house 4–12 months) on a new concern `works`, keyed by the target's lineage with the start week as the creation index, over table-exact durations, because the owner's words give ranges ("two weeks or a month") and a fixed duration per row would make every house of a class finish in step, while the keyed draw keeps the same history giving the same weeks on every host and never disturbs another concern's draws (§6.1; item 67). |
swaps.new_row: | J-A67.61 | Chose to draw a Works' timing inside its `WorksTable` row's range (a small timber house 2–6 weeks, a stone house 4–12 months) on a new concern `works`, keyed two ways — for a Works an epoch starts, by the target's lineage with the epoch's week as the creation index and the epoch component, the start offset within the epoch's span drawn first and the duration second; for a Works a dated change or a scheduled edit starts, by the target's lineage with its given start week as the creation index, the duration alone — over table-exact durations and over one key built from the start week, because the owner's words give ranges ("two weeks or a month") and a fixed duration per row would make every house of a class finish in step, while an epoch's Works draws its own start week, so a key built from that week would need the draw's result before the draw; both keys keep the same history giving the same weeks on every host and never disturb another concern's draws (§6.1; item 67; repair r1, VD0-01). |

swaps.new_row: | J-A72.61 | Chose to treat a district's character vector and band range as derived — pure functions of committed state, recomputed on load and never hashed — and its `identity`, `pressure` and `nameHistory` as model data in the digest, written by generation, by epochs and by dossier events (a district-defining institution or a matched claim sets the identity, a dossier rename extends the name history), and the identity also by a `setAttr` override, over hashing all five or deriving all five, because the vector and range can always be recomputed from the lots and the slices, while the identity depends on the epochs and dossier events it lived through (the hysteresis's dwell), the pressure is a retained accumulation and the name history a record of renames, none of which the present state alone reproduces (§6.2; item 72, ruling 7; repair r1, V-MC0-20). |

swaps.old_row: | J-A65.31 | Chose to let the underground layer hold several arenas — a `PlatKey` part per system that may pass over or under another without meeting, the sewer network keeping part 0 and each further system taking a number allocated once at its creation and never renumbered or reused, because the number is part of its entities' keys and addresses — and to carry J-A12.32 across them unchanged (a transaction writes one part; a stage reads the ground and every other part by key; a meeting of two systems, or a stair or shaft joining them, is a record that names one vertex in each part; every entity's geometry lies in the one part its `Identity.key` names, and a grouping that spans systems — an undercity neighbourhood and its outskirts along the sewer tunnels — is a link between records in different parts, over one entity with faces in two arenas, which would give `Identity` a second key and every reader of a reference a choice of arena), over grade separation inside one arena (a crossing vertex that joins nothing, or faces allowed to overlap where their depths differ), because every kernel guarantee — faces that never overlap, every crossing a vertex, nesting checked by index, `minEdge` and clearance tested against the index — rests on an arena being one planar subdivision, so an exception for depth would have to be carried through every writer, query and invariant, while a separate part costs only its index partitions, snapshot block and level digests and keeps a re-derivation of one system from touching another; it amends J-A12.45's "one underground arena" for systems and keeps its depth per entity inside each part (§3.4, §3.10; item 65 (a), (d), (e); the kernel's confirmation asked by ruling 1 of the route's item 65; amendments-c, kernel seat). |
swaps.new_row: | J-A65.31 | Chose to let the underground layer hold several arenas — a `PlatKey` part per system that may pass over or under another without meeting, the sewer network keeping part 0 and each further system taking a number allocated once at its creation and never renumbered or reused, because the number is part of its entities' keys and addresses — and to carry J-A12.32 across them unchanged (a transaction writes one part; a stage reads the ground and every other part by key; a meeting of two systems, or a stair or shaft joining them, is a record that names one vertex in each part; every entity's geometry lies in the one part its `Identity.key` names (a link's two ends excepted, one vertex in each part), and a grouping that spans systems — an undercity neighbourhood and its outskirts along the sewer tunnels — is a link between records in different parts, over one entity with faces in two arenas, which would give `Identity` a second key and every reader of a reference a choice of arena), over grade separation inside one arena (a crossing vertex that joins nothing, or faces allowed to overlap where their depths differ), because every kernel guarantee — faces that never overlap, every crossing a vertex, nesting checked by index, `minEdge` and clearance tested against the index — rests on an arena being one planar subdivision, so an exception for depth would have to be carried through every writer, query and invariant, while a separate part costs only its index partitions, snapshot block and level digests and keeps a re-derivation of one system from touching another beyond its links' far ends; it amends J-A12.45's "one underground arena" for systems and keeps its depth per entity inside each part (§3.4, §3.10; item 65 (a), (d), (e); the kernel's confirmation asked by ruling 1 of the route's item 65; amendments-c, kernel seat). |

swaps.old_row: | J-A68.21 | Chose to make a point light a record anchored on its host — kind, fire or magic, point, host (with the entrance ordinal of a door light), height, intensity in candela, radius, the flame's or orb's own size, colour and an optional flicker phase — with lit or unlit a reading of the host's state, lit windows, room lights and light shafts derived and never records, and the controls for day, night, sun and lantern per-viewer view keys with the pointer's position never stored, over storing every light including windows or storing the cursor's sun, because placed lights are things a user adds, moves and removes (the owner's torches) while lit windows follow who lives in a building and how its rooms lie, and the cursor is a way of looking, not a fact of the map. |
swaps.new_row: | J-A68.21 | Chose to make a point light a record anchored on its host — kind, fire or magic, point, host (with the entrance ordinal of a door light), height, intensity in candela, radius, the flame's or orb's own size, colour and an optional flicker flag — with lit or unlit a reading of the host's state, lit windows, room lights and light shafts derived and never records, and the controls for day, night, sun and lantern per-viewer view keys with the pointer's position never stored, over storing every light including windows or storing the cursor's sun, because placed lights are things a user adds, moves and removes (the owner's torches) while lit windows follow who lives in a building and how its rooms lie, and the cursor is a way of looking, not a fact of the map. The flicker is a flag, never a stored phase: its motion follows from the light's render key and the view's time alone (J-A68.61), so nothing is drawn for it and nothing enters the model digest. The colour is the one the light pass lights with (§8.4 (c)), and a style's `light` and `lights` roles tint only the vector rung's glyph and glow, over letting a style shift a source's colour, because §8.2's light roles are the vector rung's tones and no style rule reaches the light pass. |

swaps.old_row: | J-A65.46 | Chose to make a buried old town the conversion `raiseGrade { region; raiseCm; cause }`, by an epoch or by hand: the region's ground is raised by S1's terrain operator, its records at the old grade end on the ground (`cleared`) and their successors become the `buried` system's galleries (the old streets) and chambers (the old ground storeys) by §6.3's succession, while the ground above is re-derived regrowth-first on the old centrelines, over copying the old town into the underground or deriving buried towns at generation, because no geometry may live in two arenas at once (J-A12.43), because succession keeps each old place's history addressable, and because "the evolution log supplies it" — a settlement without that history has none, unless the staged port names such a scar (II.7.6; item 65 (b)(1), ruling 5; amendments-c, pipeline seat D). |
